pr_comments:
One further thing, the example project includes the following script:

```gd
func _ready() -> void:
    for child in self.get_children():
        # Disable speculars for all meshes
        var mesh = child as MeshInstance3D
        if mesh:
            var mat = mesh.get_active_material(0) as StandardMaterial3D
            mat.specular_mode = BaseMaterial3D.SPECULAR_DISABLED
        
        # The light is configured to have intensity of PI, which is then
        # compensated by the 1/PI normalization of the BRDF.
        # However, Godot seems to not do this?
        var light = child as Light3D
        if light:
            light.light_energy = 1.0
```

In the test case I had configured the light intensity to PI to compensate for the 1/PI factor in normalized Lambertian diffuse. The top row contains emissive colors with zero diffuse. If the light intensity is not hacked the diffuse planes are quite a bit brighter:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/3875461/fb5efbcd-93c1-43ff-bd8c-6c1de80a0b12)

Both Arnold and ufbx's test path tracer result in the correct image with the PI-intensity light, so it seems that Godot is doing something different here. FBX2glTF also seems to import the light intensity as-is, so it's probably for the best not to touch it, even though it will result in brighter scenes than in other renderers.

Also, speaking of FBX2glTF, here is what the test scene looks like using that, after the following fixes:

* Directional light was rotated by 90 degrees
* Orthographic camera units were not scaled, resulting in a 100x too large camera
* Half of the tiles use material that FBX2glTF does not support (Autodesk Standard)

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/3875461/1d0bff3c-12b8-4e94-871a-d4cd591b976f)

I couldn't get the emissive and diffuse materials to match up using FBX2glTF, either with PI-intensity and 1-intensity directional light. This does mean that ufbx will produce different results than FBX2glTF, so it might be worth it to look a bit deeper whether ufbx is doing the correct thing after all.

Follow-up observation comparing the FBX2glTF (left) and ufbx (right) result:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/3875461/c0ddd4a7-a259-48c8-b0e1-162163f6a352)

The highlighted tiles use a texture that is twice as bright and base color factor of `0.5`. It looks like FBX2glTF does take the base color factor into account by default, so for compatibility it would probably make sense to do that in the ufbx importer as well. On the other hand, many authoring programs default the base color factor to `0.8`, so users may get darker textures than they would expect, but that would already be an issue with FBX2glTF.
As long as everyone is in agreement of using the albedo factor with albedo textures, I'd say I'm fine with getting this merged as-is.

I don't know why this fails randomly, but it feels unrelated.

issue_context.title: ufbx material colors are not converted to sRGB
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.3 (using ufbx)
- Not reproducible in 4.2.x or older

### System information

Godot v4.3.dev (655e93d58) - Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.3713) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9900K CPU @ 3.60GHz (16 Threads)

### Issue description

Material colors on imported fbx seem to not be converted to srgb.
For example, the RightEar material should be color `#e711a5` but is instead imported as `#cc0160`

Note: I am not talking about vertex colors, which should be tested separately. In this issue, all of the colors on the imported fbx come strictly from materials.

It is important to fix before the release of 4.3, because otherwise we will be forced to break compat in terms of material colors in the future.

![Left: ufbx saturated/dark. Right: FBX2glTF more pastel](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/39946030/3093a199-0e95-44bd-b3d9-99dddff8f5bb)
Left side: ufbx. Right side: FBX2glTF (matches Blender)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the project. fbx_vs_ufbx_test.tscn contains two copies of the identical .fbx file: one is imported with ufbx, and the other with legacy FBX2glTF
2. The FBX2glTF version has colors which match other programs (blender, unity)
3. The ufbx version near origin has the incorrect colors, saturated and darker

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[fbx_material_sorting.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14945136/fbx_material_sorting.zip)
comments:
The code to apply the material colors is here. https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b2f425fe680d1ed5d5b5fa9ae289ae93fd294607/modules/fbx/fbx_document.cpp#L89C14-L105

Perhaps do a Color.linear_to_srgb()? https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_color.html#class-color-method-linear-to-srgb
